paper.title: Optimal Allocation Strategies for the Dark Pool Problem

settings.name_in_paper: Dark pool problem with continuous-valued (fractional) allocations, adversarial volumes and liquidities
unmapped: Censored feedback: per venue i the learner observes r_i = min(v_i, s_i), allowing a subgradient of the concave reward
Allocations v_i >= 0 with sum_i v_i <= V^t, volumes V^t in {1..V}; learner knows the volume bound V
Reward is sum_i min(v_i, s_i) (concave in allocations); comparator is best fixed unit-to-venue assignment opt in {1..K}^V
settings.definition_quote: A learning algorithm receives a sequence of volumes $\vol{1},\dots\,\vol{T}$ where $\vol{t} \in \{1,\dots,\vol{}\}$. It has $K$ available venues, amongst which it can allocate up to $\vol{t}$ units at time $t$. ... The learner then receives the number of units $\cons{i}{t} = \min(\alloc{i}{t}, \limit{i}{t})$ consumed at venue $i$. We allow the sequence of volumes and maximum consumption levels to be chosen adversarially

settings.name_in_paper: Dark pool problem with integer-valued allocations, oblivious adversary
unmapped: Integer allocations u_i >= 0 with sum_i u_i <= V^t, V^t <= V; integer liquidities s_i; censored feedback min(u_i, s_i) per venue
Learner knows the volume bound V
Comparator is best fixed unit-to-venue assignment opt in {1..K}^V; generalizes K-armed bandits (V=1)
settings.definition_quote: In this section we describe a low regret algorithm that allocates an integral number of units to each venue. ... An oblivious adversary is one that chooses $V^t$ and $s_i^t$ without seeing the algorithm's (random) allocations $u_i^t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Dark pool problem with integer-valued allocations, adaptive adversary
unmapped: Integer allocations u_i >= 0 with sum_i u_i <= V^t, V^t <= V; integer liquidities; censored feedback min(u_i, s_i) per venue
Learner knows the volume bound V
Comparator is best fixed unit-to-venue assignment opt in {1..K}^V
settings.definition_quote: We allow the sequence of volumes and maximum consumption levels to be chosen adversarially, i.e. $V_t, \limit{i}{t}$ can depend on $\{\alloc{i}{1},\dots,\alloc{i}{t-1}\}_{i=1}^K$.

algorithms.name: ExpGrad (Exponentiated gradient algorithm for continuous-valued allocations, Algorithm 1)
Algorithm 2 with variance-corrected gradient estimator g-hat

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on the per-round volume V^t

source.label: thm:regretfrac
source.quote: For any choices of the volumes $\vol{t}\in[0,V]$ and of the maximum consumption levels $\limit{i}{t}$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:fracalloc} with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{(e-2)T}}$ over $T$ rounds is $O(V\sqrt{T\ln K})$.

results.notes: Algorithm is deterministic so the bound holds for every sequence; proof gives explicit 3V sqrt(T ln K). Quantity type not named in paper.

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on the per-round volume V^t

conditions: via reduction from the experts problem with rewards in [0,V]

source.label: sec:lbcont
source.quote: Hence the optimal regret on the dark pools problem is at least $\Omega(V\sqrt{T\ln K})$. As Algorithm~\ref{alg:fracalloc} gets the same bound up to constant factors in a harder adversarial setting than used in the lower bounds, we conclude that it attains the minimax optimal regret up to constant factors.

results.notes: Not stated as a formal theorem; argued in text via reduction to experts lower bound (Haussler et al.; Abernethy et al.).

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on the per-round volume V^t

source.label: thm:regretintexp
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg:intallocexp}, with $\eta = \left(\frac{V(\ln K)^2}{KT^2}\right)^{1/3}$, has expected regret over $T$ rounds of $O((VTK)^{2/3}(\ln K)^{1/3})$, where $V$ is the bound on volumes $\vol{t}$, and the volumes and maximum consumption levels $\limit{i}{t}$ are chosen by an oblivious adversary.

results.notes: Proof ends with explicit 6(VTK)^{2/3}(ln K)^{1/3}. Efficient sampling of subset distribution deferred to full version, so compute not_stated.

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on the per-round volume V^t

source.label: thm:regretintprob
source.quote: With probability at least 1 - $\frac{1}{T}$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:intallocexp} using the gradient estimator $\gh_t$ against oblivious adversaries is $\widetilde{O}\left(V(TK)^{2/3}\right)$.

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on the per-round volume V^t

source.quote: With probability at least 1 - $\frac{1}{T}$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:intallocexp} against adaptive adversaries is $\widetilde{O}\left(V^2(TK)^{2/3}\right)$.

results.notes: Obtained by union bound over K^V comparators. Paper also says online-to-batch gives per-round suboptimality O~(V^2 T^{-1/3} K^{2/3}) in iid setting (not recorded separately).

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on the per-round volume V^t

conditions: hard instances: liquidities s_i^t = V with probability 1/2 + eps for one venue and 1/2 for others (iid)

source.label: thm:regretlbexp
source.quote: Any algorithm that plays integer valued allocations has expected regret that is $\Omega\left(\sqrt{TV(K+V\ln K)}\right).$

results.notes: Combines Omega(sqrt(TVK)) from Exp3-style construction with Omega(V sqrt(T ln K)) from fractional case. Construction is stochastic iid, so the bound holds also for iid environments.
